paper_sections.title: Effective amygdala-prefrontal connectivity predicts individual differences in successful emotion regulation
Prefrontal network underlying the down-regulation of emotion
Amygdala-prefrontal network underlying the up-regulation of emotion

description.value: The study examined whether effective connectivity between the left inferior frontal gyrus or amygdala and other emotion-regulation regions during cognitive reappraisal is associated with individual differences in reappraisal success.

spans.text: Specifically, this study examined within-subject effective connectivity ( ; ) of the IFG and the amygdala and its association with reappraisal success using fMRI and psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analysis.

design.value: Event-related functional magnetic resonance imaging study using cognitive reappraisal to increase, maintain, or decrease emotional responses, with psychophysiological interaction analyses and reappraisal success entered as an explicit predictor.

spans.text: Pictures were presented in an event-related design ( ).

Using psychophysiological interaction analyses of functional magnetic resonance imaging data, we examined changes in inter-regional connectivity between the amygdala and IFG with other brain regions during reappraisal of emotional responses and used emotion regulation success as an explicit regressor.
Stimuli consisted of 126 aversive and 42 neutral pictures from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS) ( ).
After each emotion regulation phase subjects rated their current emotional state on a scale from 1 to 4.

description.value: Participants rated their current emotional state on a four-point Likert scale from 1 to 4, from less negative to very negative.

Thus, we also recorded EDA to obtain a physiological control measure, which was expected to mirror self-reports of emotional state after emotion regulation.

Our participants were presented with highly arousing and aversive pictures while using cognitive reappraisal to increase, maintain, or decrease their emotional responses.

task_description.value: Participants viewed aversive or neutral pictures and were instructed to increase, decrease, or not manipulate their emotional responses, followed by an emotional-state rating and jittered fixation.

spans.text: The instruction was followed by the presentation of an IAPS picture for 8 s, during which subjects were asked to either up-regulate (Increase), down-regulate (Decrease) their emotions or not modulate their emotions at all (Look-Neutral, Look-Negative). After this regulation phase, subjects rated their current emotional state on a scale from 1 to 4 within 4 s. Each trial ended with a jittered fixation phase of 4–8 s.
Pictures were presented in an event-related design ( ).

During the fMRI experiment, images were presented in the centre of the screen with an 800 × 600 pixel display subtending 32° × 24° visual angle on dual display goggles (VisuaStim, MR Research, USA) using the stimulation software Presentation (Version 14.1, Neurobehavioral Systems, USA).

instructions.value: In the ‘Increase’ condition, subjects were asked to engage themselves with the depicted situation and to increase their sense of subjective closeness to the displayed events; in the ‘Decrease’ condition subjects were instructed to reduce the intensity of the negative emotion by distancing themselves from the image; in the ‘Look’ condition, subjects were asked to view the neutral or negative stimuli attentively and allow themselves to experience or feel any emotional responses without trying to manipulate them.

spans.text: (i) In the ‘Increase’ condition, subjects were asked to engage themselves with the depicted situation and to increase their sense of subjective closeness to the displayed events by e.g. imaging a close friend/family member in the situation depicted in the picture ( ; ; ). (ii) Conversely, in the ‘Decrease’ condition subjects were instructed to reduce the intensity of the negative emotion by distancing themselves from the image by becoming a detached observer e.g. through thinking that the depicted situation is not real. (iii) In the ‘Look’ condition, subjects were asked to view the neutral (‘Look-Neutral’) or negative (‘Look-Negative’) stimuli attentively and allow themselves to experience/feel any emotional responses, which these might elicit without trying to manipulate them.
